correctness.rationale: Derivatives have normalized positive real part, so Herglotz representation supplies probability measures. Coefficientwise products correspond to convolution of these measures and an explicit positive kernel. The angular kernel derivative s(1-s^2)/(1-2s cos(theta)+s^2)^2 proves the global minimum at -r; point masses attain it. Radial strict decrease and exact boundary moments 1-log2 and 1-pi^2/12 prove the full phase classification, including equality at the limiting disk boundary. The included checker validates rational coefficient identities and selected numerical boundary tests; the theorem is analytical.

value.rationale: The 2022 convolution theorem guarantees stability when one factor is convex, leaving the natural bounded-turning-by-bounded-turning case open to separate analysis. This result provides its complete sharp filtration entry parameter and its nontrivial radius-vs-parameter phase diagram, with a single explicitly extremizing pair. It identifies when two coefficientwise positive-derivative maps produce a semigroup generator in the strictly smaller prescribed filtration class, a structural closure question rather than an isolated numerical example.
